items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: And Bill Davison came to town with a band with Pee Wee and Brad Gowans and James P. Johnson and Kaiser Marshall.

ctx.x: Did you hear Pee Wee in Boston? No, not at that age.

Yeah, as a matter of fact I did. I heard him at a place called, it was called the Ken Club. This was during the war. And Bill Davison came to town with a band with Pee Wee and Brad Gowans and James P. Johnson and Kaiser Marshall. It was quite a band. He was also a guitar player. That's right, Jack Goss. Yeah, I remember. I wish I could hear that band again.

Well, strangely enough, Bill wrote to me from Boston and said, this is the best band I ever had, you ought to record us. At that time I was interested in records. And I knew the small chances I'd have of getting Bill to record the band himself. But I wrote back and said, is there a good studio in Boston and do you want to record a couple sides? Let me hear what they're like. And he said, yes, for $10 we can go in for an hour. So I sent him the $10. Of course nothing ever happened. I didn't hear the band. But they…
